newsitem.title: USA: USDA pegs 1996/97 cotton crop at 18.738 mln bales.
newsitem.headline: USDA pegs 1996/97 cotton crop at 18.738 mln bales.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's December cotton supply and demand data could jolt the market out of its current trading range, as higher exports and lower ending stocks were forecast from last month, analysts said.

The USDA's estimate of 18.738 million bales for the 1996/97 cotton crop, however, is not likely to sway the market by itself, as the forecast was within the range of analysts' expectations. The crop would be the third largest in U.S. history, the USDA said.
Industry sources had pegged the crop estimate between 18.6 million and 18.788 million bales, up slightly from 18.59 million bales forecast last month.

The USDA put exports at 6.2 million bales for the season, compared with 5.8 million bales in November. While new sales for the week ended Dec 5 were a mere 45,300 bales, and new commitments only 38,300 bales, cuts in foreign crops justify higher exports in the longer term.
"When it's all said and done, the world is down a million bales. That's why the USDA raised exports," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
Cuts came in Pakistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Australia, and Brazil.
U.S. ending stocks fell to 4.6 million bales versus 4.9 last month, and imports were lowered to 450,000 bales from 500,000 bales last month.
Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said the USDA report would be constructive for prices in the near term. "The higher crop was more than offset by (higher) exports," she said.
Johnson said prices would react initially but added the market cannot afford to stay higher for very long if the U.S. is going to reach its current export target.
NYCE cotton futures settled slightly lower on Wednesday, with March easing 0.36 cent on the day to 76.17 cents per pound, traded 76.45 to 76.10 cents.
